## 1) Select best module candidate (AUB)
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_autopilot.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --run --select-best
```
What to check after it finishes:
- It should emit which module/version was selected as “best” and where it wrote results (typically under `baseline/reports/` or an experiment output dir).
- Confirm it did **not** downgrade the current champion unintentionally. If it updates `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json` (or a symlink/alias), verify the reported metrics improved (or at least meet your promotion criteria).

If it errors:
- Common causes are missing deps, registry YAML path issues, or a candidate config failing tests. Re-run with whatever verbose/log flag the tool supports (often `--verbose` / `--debug`), or inspect the last log file it points to.

## 2) Run system-level candidates
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/system_autopilot.py \
  --spec experiment_system/config/system_candidates.yaml \
  --run
```
What to check:
- This should evaluate system configurations (not just modules). Confirm:
  - Which candidates were run
  - Any failures/timeouts
  - The ranking/selection summary (and whether anything is marked PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE)
- If it produces a “best system” artifact, confirm whether it updates any “current system” pointer/config or just reports.

## 3) Generate the “next fix” report
```bash
python3 experiment_system/tools/aub_next_fix.py \
  --registry experiment_system/config/module_registry.yaml \
  --output baseline/reports/next_fix.md
```
What to check:
- `baseline/reports/next_fix.md` should contain actionable items (e.g., which candidates are close to passing, what metrics/regressions block promotion).
- If it’s empty or unhelpful, it usually means:
  - No recent runs were found/registered
  - Output paths don’t match what the reporting tool expects

## Minimal sanity checks (fast)
- Ensure `baseline/champion_v5_latest.json` still exists and is valid JSON.
- Confirm the reported means/mins you care about (tuning and lockbox) are improving vs:

- Verify any promoted “best” is actually evaluated on the same dataset/seed settings as the champion (to avoid apples-to-oranges).

If you paste the stdout summaries from each command (or the paths of the generated reports), I can tell you whether the run looks consistent and what to do next (e.g., promote, rerun with constraints, or isolate a failing candidate).
